# US tariffs dent vehicle growth at Brunswick in 2025

With the introduction of US tariffs in 2025, automakers paused shipments, closed factories and held volumes at ports, leading to a year-on-year reduction in import and export volumes at the Port of Brunswick in Georgia.

Marcus Williams Marcus Williams

results.title: Georgia Ports Authority weathers year of tariffs with strong performance
results.content:
Compared to 2024, GPA saw a 7.5% decline in 2025 volume at the Port of Brunswick, its Roll-On/Roll-Off port for autos and heavy machinery. The drop in volume was driven by tariffs that led to some manufacturers pausing shipments and a decline in exports to China, according to GPA. [...] Still the authority is moving forward with major capital projects in Brunswick, namely a fourth shipping berth that is now 15% complete, Lynch said. Lynch also expressed moderated expectations for the close of the fiscal year, while noting that shipping customers are anticipating a strong end to the 2026 calendar year.

Lynch noted that U.S. Gross Domestic Product is still strong and consumer spending continued modest increases at the end of 2025, according to federal statistics. [...] The growth was anchored by early year gains in February, March and April, when shippers were moving large amounts of cargo ahead of the anticipated tariffs. Those same gains contributed to GPA having its second busiest fiscal year on record, although tariffs caused dips in volume in June and October.
